title: Hearty Braised Chinese Pork Bao
description: A savory and mustardy Chinese dish featuring braised pork and sauerkraut, perfect for a brunch mood, this recipe is kosher-friendly and serves as a great option for those looking for a unique meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large Dutch oven, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Sear the pork shoulder until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes per side.
Remove the pork from the pot and set it aside.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the sauerkraut, brown sugar, soy sauce, and rice vinegar to the pot, stirring to combine.
Return the pork to the pot and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Cover the pot and transfer it to the preheated oven, braising the pork for 2 1/2 hours, or until tender.
While the pork is braising, toast the bao buns by baking them in the oven for 5 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Assemble the bao by slicing the braised pork and serving it in the toasted buns with a spoonful of the sauerkraut mixture and a dollop of mustard.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before serving.
